answer: A velvet rope guards the bracket: only identities staking one onyx chip of 70 credits enter. A random beacon wanders the draw, so no identity can pick a weak opponent. Paired agents file one proof; the loser forfeits its chip, the winner advances. An attacker fielding 1,000 fakes pays 70,000 credits, mostly facing itself and burning its chips. A rented player throwing a match loses its own chip. An honest agent pays 70 once and keeps its share.
